messages:
Alex (Customer): Hey team — hitting a weird failure on the embeddings endpoint. We used the embeddings API to index a batch from our client and we started getting "dimension mismatch" errors. Sample error: 422 Unprocessable Entity - embeddings: dimension mismatch (expected 1536, got 512). We definitely never changed the model, we call model="rwd-embed-1536". Request id: rwd_req_01HXYZA3. Timestamp: 2024-06-16T09:07:00Z. Anyone seen this?

Maya (Support): sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact request body you sent (no secrets) and the SDK/language? Also does the error happen for a single text input or only when batching?

Alex (Customer): Repro steps below. We're using Python requests from a microservice that pulls precomputed tokens from a transformer encoder (512-d float array) and then posts to /v1/embeddings expecting the service to accept vectors for similarity. Example payload we used: 

```json
{
  "model": "rwd-embed-1536",
  "input": [[0.12, 0.3, ... 512 floats ...]]
}
```

We were under the impression the embeddings endpoint accepts raw vectors for indexing. Error returns immediately. If we instead send a single string text, it works and returns a 1536-d vector.

Priya (ML Eng): quick clarification — Redwood's embeddings endpoint expects text input (string or list of strings) and returns model-generated vectors. It doesn't accept precomputed vectors as payload. If you POST a nested array of floats to the text embeddings endpoint, the service tries to treat that array as tokenized text (or tries to parse JSON schema) and you can end up with dimension errors. The "expected 1536 got 512" happens because the model's output embedding dim is 1536; the server tried to validate shape and failed.

Alex (Customer): ahhh ok that explains it. Two followups: 1) Is there a way to send precomputed vectors for storage/nearest neighbor indexing via the API? 2) Why did this only start after we added a batching layer in front of our client (we use a micro-batcher that groups 4 inputs)?

Maya (Support): 1) We don't allow direct ingestion of arbitrary float vectors into the embeddings generation endpoint. For index storage we provide a separate ingest route (private-dedicated customers) or recommend storing vectors in your vector DB directly. If you need Redwood to store them, open a feature request with your account rep.

2) Batching can mask shape issues — if your micro-batcher wraps things twice (e.g., you send [[[...floats...]]]) the server will see an extra nesting level and try to interpret it as multiple inputs. Common client mistakes: sending a single item as a nested list ("input": [[text]] vs "input": [text]) or passing numpy arrays serialized with .tolist() incorrectly (shape (1,512) vs (512,)).

Daniel (Devex): adding some concrete repro tips — here's a minimal Python example that WILL fail if you try to send precomputed floats to the generation endpoint: 

```python
import requests
url = "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/embeddings"
headers = {
  "Authorization": "Bearer <REDACTED>",
  "Content-Type": "application/json"
}
body = {
  "model": "rwd-embed-1536",
  "input": [[0.1, 0.2, 0.3] * 170]  # incorrect: precomputed floats, not text
}
res = requests.post(url, json=body, headers=headers)
print(res.status_code, res.text)
```

Expected server response when shape mismatch: 
```
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
{"error":"embeddings: dimension mismatch (expected 1536, got 512)"}
```

Priya (ML Eng): If you actually want to embed client text, send text or list of strings. Examples: 

Python correct (single): 
```python
body = {
  "model": "rwd-embed-1536",
  "input": "loan application denied, why?"
}
```
Python correct (batch): 
```python
body = {
  "model": "rwd-embed-1536",
  "input": ["first text", "second text", "third text"]
}
```
JS (common pitfall): people sometimes call with a single string but wrap it as an array of arrays: 
```js
// BAD: nested arrays cause schema mismatch
fetch('/v1/embeddings', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'rwd-embed-1536', input: [["text"]] }) })
// GOOD:
fetch('/v1/embeddings', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'rwd-embed-1536', input: ["text"] }) })
```

Maya (Support): also check content-type — if your batching layer accidentally sends application/x-www-form-urlencoded or sends a stringified numpy array (like "array([...])") the server won't parse it as JSON and you'll get a 400 with weird body. Attach logs if possible.

Alex (Customer): thanks, we did find one issue: our Go micro-batcher serialized a []float32 as a JSON string payload instead of a JSON array because of a bug in our serializer. So the body looked like "input:" : "[0.1,0.2,0.3]" (a string), which the server then treated as text and attempted tokenization resulting in unexpected behaviour. Fixed that.

Priya (ML Eng): nice catch. A few extra tips to avoid future shape/encoding problems: 
- Always validate client-side shapes before sending (ensure arrays are 1-d for floats, or use string/text inputs).
- Use the SDKs where possible (they enforce schema).
- If you maintain a batching proxy, add schema checks at ingress (e.g., ensure typeof input === 'string' or Array.isArray(input) && typeof input[0] === 'string').
- For throughput: avoid sending too large batches to the hosted endpoint; we recommend batch sizes of 8-32 for text inputs depending on average length and model. Sending thousands of strings in one request will be rate-limited or time out.

Daniel (Devex): adding a quick snippet to canonicalize inputs server-side (JS): 
```js
function normalizeInput(input) {
  if (typeof input === 'string') return [input];
  if (!Array.isArray(input)) throw new Error('input must be string or array of strings');
  // flatten once if nested accidentally
  if (Array.isArray(input[0])) input = input.flat();
  if (!input.every(x => typeof x === 'string')) throw new Error('all inputs must be strings');
  return input;
}
```

Maya (Support): small note on billing/alerts — failed requests still count toward your request quota in some retry scenarios, and repeated errors flooded the customer's billing alerts. If you see unexpected bill increases from retries, we can review logs and disable automated retry flaps on our side for a short window.

Alex (Customer): we did see a spike because our batcher retried idempotently 5x on failures. We fixed the serialization and reduced retries. After that things look normal.

deploy-bot: deploy rwd/support-fix-validate-inputs succeeded in 2m 18s — validation added to our support proxy to catch nested arrays and stringified arrays earlier.

Maya (Support): glad that's resolved. If you want, share your request_id logs and we'll confirm there were no downstream side effects (quota/billing). Also happy to queue a feature request for a dedicated vector ingestion API for customers who want to push precomputed embeddings. :thumbsup:

Alex (Customer): thanks everyone — appreciate the quick turnaround. Confirming resolved on our end.
